touches.text: Evidence, a measurement, says what is. It settles what it measures, for everyone. Why? Because evidence ALWAYS wins.
Questions live here and nowhere else. The questions/ inbox and `cairn question` are deprecated for now. -amm
TICKET (a machine, and the class every kind of ticket inherits from; a first class object)
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.

question: the open-question door: a decision only the operator can make, bound to its ticket, answered in the operator's words. WHY: a spec choice is settled by Akien's head, recorded verbatim, never by a paragraph of CC's. USERS: tickets and CodeMother open them; the operator answers (7.4.2).

dataref: one address for any stored record, in any format, and the thin class that reads it. WHY: a config, a ticket or a node can say WHERE a value lives without carrying it, so the repo stays shareable and a private value stays in ~/.cairn; and one way of pointing works across every format and every box. USERS: anything that reads stored data.

The scheme names the root; the path finds the record; the part after # finds the item inside it. Each root is found on the box it runs on, so one address works on Linux, on Windows and on a fresh machine.

cairn:/// is the repo (from the environment, or from where bin/cairn itself lives); cairncommons:/// is the commons repo beside it; instance:/// is ~/.cairn; claude:/// is ~/.claude (the project's own .claude/ is already cairn:///.claude/, so it gets no second name); db:///cairn/table/row is the database; file:/// keeps its usual meaning, a real path on the filesystem, for what no root holds. claude: is also the Claude app's link scheme on this box: the resolver never hands an address to the system, so only a click on one opens the app.

QUESTIONS: a question is [Q#n: ...], placed at the line it bears on. Its #n is its own and never changes; a new one takes the next unused number, which is now 127. An answered question disappears: its answer is folded into the intention and why (0.2.1), and signed where it records a decision (0.5). Why? Becuase too many words makes it hard for both akien and Claude to understand.

The plan is <id>-<slug>.json: current, one-line outcomes and constraints. The history is <id>.log.jsonl, append-only. Questions live in the outline (0.6.2). A big decision goes in these files; a small one on the ticket.
Knowledge: one list of nodes, owned by the librarian.
Transient: things held for seconds to days (mail, logs, test runs, trouble tickets, inference tickets). The logging tree.

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.
